From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: HIPAA / BAA eligibility — follow-up and SOC2/docs

Hi Sofia / Alan —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep the procurement/security loop moving: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary use case: clinical notes enrichment and coding assistance (near-real-time inference).
- PHI surface: patient identifiers, clinical notes, limited demographic data.
- Volume: pilot ~50k API requests/day, production target ~500k/day.
- Key security asks: BAA availability, SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration, data retention and audit logs.

What Redwood can confirm up front:
- We support BAAs for customers who need to process PHI, but PHI processing must occur on isolated tenancy (Dedicated or Private deployments).
  - Private (VPC / on-prem) = fully supported for PHI and eligible for a standard BAA.
  - Dedicated (reserved GPU pools / dedicated tenancy) = supported for PHI; we provide a BAA and can integrate with your KMS/HSM.
  - Hosted/shared API (multi-tenant) = not eligible for PHI processing. We do not recommend sending PHI to shared hosted endpoints and cannot sign a BAA for shared tenancy.

Attachments: I attached our latest SOC 2 report and our standard BAA template for your legal/security team to review. (See attachments list.)

Next steps I propose:
1) Please confirm whether MedCare will proceed on Dedicated or Private for the pilot/production.
2) Alan — if you can drop the vendor security questionnaire link (or attach the doc), I’ll loop in our security team (Rishi) to complete it.
3) If legal wants edits to the BAA, we can route to our legal team; we often exchange a redline and finalize via DocuSign.

I’m looping Rishi and Monica on this thread for the questionnaire + implementation details. Happy to set a short follow-up call next week.

Thanks,
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0198

Marissa — thanks for the recap and for sending the SOC2/BAA template. A few clarifying Qs from our security team before we push to legal: 

1) SOC 2: can you confirm the report date and whether the report includes both CC1 and CC2? Also, do you have any complementary penetration test summaries?
2) Encryption: is data encrypted at rest and in transit by default? For rest, do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or only provider-managed?
3) PHI boundaries: you mentioned Dedicated/Private are eligible — can you confirm whether any telemetry or logs from the inference runtime ever contain PHI (e.g., request/response stored in logs, traces)? How long are logs retained by default?
4) Key management: do you support bringing your own keys (BYOK) and integration with AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault or only our keys via HSM for Private?
5) Incident response / breach notification SLA — what is your timeline for notifying customers?
6) BAA: our legal team will likely redline — will Redwood sign our BAA with standard carve-outs for subprocessing disclosures?

I attached the vendor security questionnaire (separate file) — can your security team complete and return? If it’s easier, we can schedule a 30-min deep-dive with your security/infra folks.

Thanks,
Alan

--
Alan Chu
Security Lead, MedCare Health

Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA eligibility — follow-up and SOC2/docs

Alan — great questions. Looping in Rishi (security) and Monica (Solutions/CS) to own the questionnaire and provide the technical details. Quick notes while they take a look: 

- SOC 2: the attached report is our most recent Type II (period ended 2025-12-31). It covers the core controls for security and availability; I’ve included the cover page in the attachment. Rishi — please confirm scope specifics below.
- Encryption: traffic is TLS 1.2+ in transit and we encrypt data at rest. For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault integrations; for Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs and on-prem key stores.
- Logs / telemetry: we do not persist request/response payloads containing PHI in our long-term service logs when running on Dedicated/Private. Short-lived tracing/diagnostic buffers may exist during processing but are not persisted to external observability stores. Default log retention is 30 days for service logs; this can be adjusted under enterprise contracts.
- Incident response: we have a 72-hour initial notification SLA for confirmed security incidents; full incident reports follow per contract.
- BAA: Redwood is willing to sign a BAA. For Hosted/shared tenancy, we cannot accept PHI and cannot sign BAAs for shared endpoints. Our legal team is generally receptive to customer redlines; we’ll route through DocuSign once legal has a proposed redline.

Rishi / Monica — can you pick this up? Alan/Sofia: if you can upload the vendor questionnaire to the link in the HubSpot ticket or send it back here, Rishi will start populating it and propose a 30-min call to go over any tricky items.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA eligibility — follow-up and SOC2/docs

Alan / Sofia — Rishi here (InfoSec). Thanks for the thoughtful questions — I pulled together answers inline below. Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

"1) SOC 2: can you confirm the report date and whether the report includes both CC1 and CC2? Also, do you have any complementary penetration test summaries?"
- Our Type II report covers the period ending 2025-12-31 and includes the applicable Trust Services Criteria for Security and Availability (commonly referenced as CC1/CC2 in questionnaires). We can also provide a recent penetration test summary (redacted findings) under an NDA; I’ve attached the SOC2 cover and can share the PT summary after an NDA.

"2) Encryption: is data encrypted at rest and in transit by default? For rest, do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) or only provider-managed?"
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced. At rest: yes, encrypted by default. For Dedicated customers we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS/GCP/Azure). For Private/on-prem we support BYOK via HSM integration. For hosted/shared tenancy keys are provider-managed.

"3) PHI boundaries: you mentioned Dedicated/Private are eligible — can you confirm whether any telemetry or logs from the inference runtime ever contain PHI (e.g., request/response stored in logs, traces)? How long are logs retained by default?"
- We do not persist request/response PHI to our long-term log stores when running on Dedicated/Private. Transient request buffers exist in-memory for inference but are not written to disk in those deployments. Default operational logs are retained 30 days; audit logs for Dedicated/Private can be configured to meet your retention requirements (including streaming to your SIEM).

"4) Key management: do you support bringing your own keys (BYOK) and integration with AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault or only our keys via HSM for Private?"
- Yes — Dedicated supports cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) BYOK. Private supports HSM / on-prem key stores.

"5) Incident response / breach notification SLA — what is your timeline for notifying customers?"
- Standard initial notification is within 72 hours for confirmed incidents. We provide a full incident report and remediation timeline per the contract. We can discuss shorter SLAs as part of an enterprise addendum.

"6) BAA: our legal team will likely redline — will Redwood sign our BAA with standard carve-outs for subprocessing disclosures?"
- We will review and generally accept reasonable redlines. We do require disclosure of subprocessors and will negotiate standard subprocessor clauses. For expedited handling, please send the redline to legal@redwoodinference.com and we’ll route back via DocuSign.

Next steps (proposed):
- Alan — please upload the vendor questionnaire to the HubSpot ticket (ID included in links) or attach it here.
- We can schedule a 30-min technical Q&A next week (Rishi + infra + Monica) to walk through KMS, logs, and deployment options.
- If you confirm Dedicated vs Private decision for pilot, Monica will create an implementation plan and provide lead times for Dedicated capacity or Private on-prem packaging.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Information Security, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
